metadata.title: Vehicle Data and Dealer SaaS Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How VWE's platform must change under RDW dependency, free data, channel consolidation, tax change, EV growth, acquisitions and privacy pressure.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: Each product calls the RDW and partner sources directly, keeps its own customer accounts and price lists, and hard-codes BPM rules and portal feeds.
metadata.residualArchitecture: A cached RDW register and transaction retry queue, a shared specification/history/valuation core, a portal-neutral publish queue, versioned BPM rules, shared identity and billing across brands, and a licence register enforced at every data interface.

stressors.name: RDW channel unavailable for a day or changes provider terms
stressors.detection: RDW incident notices, certificate expiry, new provider conditions.
stressors.attractor: Every product stops at once: no plate data, no transactions, angry dealers on delivery day.
stressors.businessReaction: Cache register data, queue transactions with ordered retry, publish status, and keep provider compliance current.
stressors.residue: A register cache with freshness flags, a transaction retry queue and a licence register that encode RDW terms.

stressors.name: Free RDW open data and AI apps commoditise plate lookups
stressors.detection: Growth of free plate apps; falling Finnik conversion; vendor price pressure.
stressors.attractor: Basic data revenue erodes; consumers and vendors stop paying for what is free.
stressors.businessReaction: Shift value to history, valuation, workflow and transactions; bundle data into modules.
stressors.residue: Products priced on derived intelligence and workflow rather than raw register fields.

stressors.name: A consolidated portal group bundles its own dealer tools
stressors.detection: Portal acquisitions (AutoScout24 with AutoTrack and Gaspedaal), new portal pricing and dealer tool launches.
stressors.attractor: Portals restrict feeds or undercut stock and pricing tools; dealers ask why they need VWE.
stressors.businessReaction: Keep syndication portal-neutral, strengthen market data independent of one portal, deepen dossier and RDW workflow.
stressors.residue: Channel adapters isolated behind a publish queue and a market data lake fed by many sources.

stressors.name: BPM rules change sharply (e.g. EV tax shift or import reform)
stressors.detection: Tax plan announcements and Belastingdienst guidance.
stressors.attractor: Import margins and calculators become wrong overnight; traders face corrections.
stressors.businessReaction: Release versioned BPM rule sets before effective dates and flag affected open cases.
stressors.residue: A versioned BPM rules engine shared by calculator, taxation reports and export refunds.

stressors.name: Used EVs become a large share of stock
stressors.detection: EV share in trade-ins and adverts; battery questions in leads.
stressors.attractor: Valuations ignore battery health; buyers distrust used EVs; stand-time rises.
stressors.businessReaction: Battery health certificates in appraisals, adverts and valuations.
stressors.residue: Battery health as a first-class input to valuation and history.

stressors.name: New owner drives buy-and-build integrations
stressors.detection: Main Capital majority stake; acquisitions like XRAY.
stressors.attractor: Each acquired brand keeps its own accounts, billing and data, multiplying cost and confusing customers.
stressors.businessReaction: Integrate identities, billing and the vehicle data core first; keep brands on the surface.
stressors.residue: Shared accounts, entitlements, billing and data core with brand-specific front ends.

stressors.name: Regulator challenges use of owner-related data for lead scoring
stressors.attractor: Lead lists and enrichment must stop or change; reputational damage.
stressors.businessReaction: Purpose limitation, pseudonymisation and audit logging for every owner-related data use.
stressors.residue: A licence and purpose register enforced at every data interface.
